142	cascade inverse would have *deleted* the memory when a plan is removed, the opposite of the intent.
143	Enum/payload typed accessors mirror `Goal`/`Units`/`HistoryEntry.sets`. Predicate captures

180	## Iteration 4 — 2026-07-02 ~11:40 — Claude Fable 5 — Item B1
181	
182	**Item:** B1. Progression engine (deterministic core) — increase load / increase reps / hold /
183	deload with a reason, math in code, not the model.
184	
185	**What changed:**
186	- NEW `Replog/Domain/ProgressionEngine.swift` — pure double-progression rule table:
187	  - `ProgressionAction` (`increaseLoad`/`increaseReps`/`hold`/`deload`, `displayName`) and
188	    `ProgressionRecommendation` (`exId`, `action`, `suggestedWeightKg`, `suggestedReps`,
189	    one-sentence `reason` ready for the B2 log card / a B3 `CoachingLog`).
190	  - `recommend(exId:history:repRange:weightStepKg:units:)` — rules, first match wins:
191	    (1) bodyweight lift (topW 0) trends on **reps** (stored e1RM is weight-based, always 0)
192	    — +1 rep uncapped, or hold on a rep stall/regression, never a weight suggestion;
193	    (2) rep-range top reached → +1 weight step, reps reset to the range floor;
194	    (3) e1RM dropped 2 consecutive deltas → deload; (4) no e1RM improvement across
195	    3 deltas → plateau deload; (5) single down session → hold (noise, not a trend);
196	    (6) otherwise +1 rep (clamped into the range).
197	  - `deloadWeight(fromKg:stepKg:)` — ~10% off, snapped to the stepper increment, always
198	    strictly below the current weight, floored at 0.
199	  - `repRange(for goal:)` — 8–12 hypertrophy/recomp, 12–15 fat loss, 6–10 sport (brackets
200	    `PlanGenerator`'s fixed 10/13/8); goal+units convenience reuses `Formulas.weightStepKg`
201	    and formats reasons via `Formulas.formatWeight` in the user's display units.
202	- FIX `Replog/Models/Coaching.swift` — `CoachingPayload` is now `nonisolated`: a clean full
203	  build surfaced 2 Swift-6 warnings from iter 3 (MainActor-isolated Codable conformance used
204	  inside nonisolated JSONDecoder/JSONEncoder generics — the custom `init(from:)` suppressed
205	  the usual nonisolated synthesis). Behavior unchanged; all 14 CoachingLog tests still green.
206	- NEW `ReplogTests/ProgressionEngineTests.swift` — 21 tests: empty/single-session/order-
207	  invariance; progressing (+rep, range-top +load & reset, above-top, below-floor lift);
208	  priority (range top beats a regressing trail); off-day hold; 2-drop regression deload;
209	  4-session flat plateau deload; 3-session flat still pushes reps; dip-then-recovery is not
210	  a regression; bodyweight rep progression past the range top + bodyweight stall holds;
211	  deload snapping/strict-below (property-swept 2.5–200 kg)/zero-step/zero-weight; goal rep
212	  ranges bracket the generator prescription; goal convenience; lb step + lb-formatted reasons.
213	
214	**Build:** clean, 0 errors / 0 warnings (** BUILD SUCCEEDED **) — after fixing the two
215	pre-existing iter-3 warnings above.
216	**Tests:** 211/211 passed on iPhone 17 (was 190; +21, all logic-layer). Every rule branch,
217	both deload reasons, both bodyweight paths and all `deloadWeight` edges are exercised.
218	
219	**Screenshots:** none — pure Domain addition, no UI surface yet (that's B2).
220	
221	**Assumptions / decisions:**
222	1. **Double progression** is the model: reps climb at fixed weight; load rises only when the
223	   goal's rep-range top is hit (then reps reset to the floor). Thresholds as named constants:
224	   `regressionDeltas = 2` (e1RM strictly down), `plateauDeltas = 3` (no improvement),
225	   `deloadFactor = 0.9`.
226	2. **Hitting the range top beats a bad trend** — reaching the top IS current success even if
227	   prior sessions regressed (tested).
228	3. **Bodyweight lifts trend on reps, not e1RM** — stored e1RM is `weight × (1 + reps/30)` = 0
229	   at 0 kg, so an e1RM-based stall signal would mark ANY 4-session bodyweight trail a plateau.
230	   Caught by hand-verifying test expectations; rep-delta logic added. Bodyweight stalls hold
231	   (form/quality cue) rather than "deload" a weight that doesn't exist.
232	4. The engine is **per-lift and history-in, recommendation-out pure**; no CoachingLog writes
233	   (that wiring is B3's acceptance) and no windowing — callers pass the (already relevant)
234	   entries, matching `ProgressAggregator`'s contract.
235	5. A single down session recommends **hold**, not deload — one bad day is noise; the reason
236	   string says so.
237	
238	**NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW:** none for this item — pure tested math. (Standing item from iters 1–3:
239	the live Apple Intelligence planner path still can't run in the simulator; verify on device.)
240	
241	**Recommended next item:** B2 (apply recommendations to the next session — surface
242	`ProgressionRecommendation` on the log card without overwriting user input). It is READY,
243	consumes B1 directly, and its acceptance (suggestion visible + dismissible + seeded-launch
244	screenshot) is the first user-visible payoff of the adaptive trainer. B3 is also READY if a
245	smaller item is preferred.

251	**Item:** B2. Apply recommendations to the next session — surface the B1 suggestion on the
252	log card, dismissible, never auto-overwriting user input.
253	
254	**What changed:**
255	- `Replog/Models/Session.swift` — `SessionExercise` gains persisted suggestion state
256	  (additive optionals + defaulted Bool → lightweight-migration safe): `suggestionActionRaw`,
257	  `suggestedWeightKg`, `suggestedReps`, `suggestionReason`, `suggestionDismissed`; a typed
258	  `suggestion: ProgressionRecommendation?` accessor (the `kindRaw`/`kind` house pattern);
259	  and `applySuggestion()` — copies the prescription onto **not-done sets only** (logged
260	  sets are never touched) and retires the banner. Stored on the session (not recomputed in
261	  the view) so suggestion + dismissal survive pause/resume.
262	- `Replog/Domain/SessionBuilder.swift` — `start` reads goal (`userProfile()`) + units
263	  (`appSettings()`) once, fetches each exercise's history once (reused for prev-fill and
264	  the engine), and stores `ProgressionEngine.recommend(…)` per exercise. No history → nil
265	  → no banner.
266	- `Replog/Features/ActiveSession/ExerciseLogCard.swift` — new private `SuggestionBanner`
267	  between header and set rows, shown while `suggestion != nil && !dismissed && !isDone`:
268	  action-tinted (up-green for increase load/reps, accent for hold, down-red for deload),
269	  SF Symbol + "Coach: <action>", the engine's reason sentence, an **Apply** capsule
270	  (opt-in; calls `applySuggestion()`), and an ✕ dismiss — both save via the existing
271	  `onChange` path and animate `.snappy` like the rest of the card.
272	- `ReplogTests/ActiveSessionTests.swift` — 8 new tests: builder attaches exactly what the
273	  engine recommends; no history → no suggestion; goal-aware (fat-loss range top → +load at
274	  62.5 kg, reps reset to 12); persistence round-trip; apply updates only undone sets and
275	  retires the banner; apply with no suggestion is a no-op; dismissal persists while the
276	  stored suggestion remains; typed-accessor round-trip incl. nil clearing.
277	
278	**Build:** clean, 0 errors / 0 warnings (`** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`).
279	**Tests:** 218/218 passed on iPhone 17 (`** TEST SUCCEEDED **`, 0 failures; +8 new,
280	`ActiveSessionTests` 8 → 16). Note: iter 4 recorded the baseline as 211, but the distinct
281	passing-test count before + after this change reconciles to 210 + 8 = 218 — the 211 appears
282	to have been an off-by-one in that log's counting, not a removed test.
283	
284	**Screenshots:** `autopilot/replog-b2-active.png` (iPhone 17) and `replog-b2-promax.png`
285	(17 Pro Max), both `REPLOG_SEED=1 REPLOG_ACTIVE=1`: the history-seeded first exercise shows
286	the green "Coach: Add a rep" banner ("Progressing well — aim for 78kg × 9.") with Apply/✕;
287	the no-history exercises show no banner; prescribed sets remain 16 kg × 10 (nothing
288	auto-overwritten); no clipping on either size. The installed iOS 26.5 runtime has no
289	SE-class device, so the small-device check used the regular 6.3" 17 (banner is flexible
290	HStack/VStack, no magic widths).
291	
292	**Assumptions / decisions:**
293	1. Suggestion is computed **at session build** and persisted on `SessionExercise`, not
294	   recomputed live: writes stay in the Domain builder (house rule), the banner is stable
295	   across pause/resume, and dismissal is per-session state — exactly the acceptance's
296	   "dismissible".
297	2. The engine receives the lift's **full history** (same data the prev-fill uses), not a
298	   recency window — consistent with the existing "previous" column; windowing/staleness
299	   policy belongs to B3 (plateau detection) if needed.
300	3. **Apply is opt-in and partial-safe**: it never touches a set the user marked done, and
301	   applying dismisses the banner (accepting the advice retires it). Dismiss keeps the
302	   stored suggestion (hidden), useful later for B3/D1 analytics.
303	4. "Hold" suggestions also get an Apply button — repeating last session's exact load/reps
304	   is still a concrete prescription when the template differs.
305	5. In the DEBUG seed, the suggested 78 kg differs wildly from the 16 kg template — that is
306	   a seed-data artifact (fabricated history at 70–78 kg vs a freshly generated plan), not
307	   an engine bug; real users' templates converge on their logged numbers.
308	
309	**NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW:**
310	- Feel-level check on device: banner animation when dismissing/applying mid-workout, and
311	  whether the banner competes visually with the rest timer bar (screenshots can't judge
312	  motion). (Standing item from iters 1–4: the live Apple Intelligence planner path still
313	  can't run in the simulator; verify on device.)
314	
315	**Recommended next item:** B3 (plateau + deload detection recorded to `CoachingLog`). It is
316	READY, builds directly on B1's rule table and A3's `recordCoaching(.plateau/.deload, …)`
317	write path, and is the last B-epic piece before the report epics (D1 consumes its logs).

2	//  ProgressionEngine.swift
3	//  Replog
4	//
5	//  The deterministic core of the adaptive trainer: given one lift's logged history,
6	//  recommend what to do next session — add load, add reps, hold, or deload — with a
7	//  human-readable reason. Classic double progression: work up the rep range at a fixed
8	//  weight, add load when the top is reached, back off when the estimated 1RM regresses
9	//  or plateaus. All math lives here in code; the AI model never prescribes numbers.
10	//
11	
12	import Foundation
13	
14	/// What the trainer recommends for the next session of a lift.
15	enum ProgressionAction: String, Codable, CaseIterable, Sendable {
16	    case increaseLoad, increaseReps, hold, deload
17	
18	    var displayName: String {
19	        switch self {
20	        case .increaseLoad: return "Add weight"
21	        case .increaseReps: return "Add a rep"
22	        case .hold:         return "Repeat"
23	        case .deload:       return "Deload"
24	        }
25	    }
26	}
27	
28	/// A concrete next-session prescription for one lift, with the coach's reasoning.
29	struct ProgressionRecommendation: Equatable, Sendable {
30	    var exId: String
31	    var action: ProgressionAction
32	    /// Suggested working weight, stored in kg like every weight in the app.
33	    var suggestedWeightKg: Double
34	    var suggestedReps: Int
35	    /// One-sentence coach explanation, ready for the log card or a `CoachingLog`.
36	    var reason: String
37	}
38	
39	enum ProgressionEngine {
40	
41	    /// Deload target as a fraction of the last working weight (~10% off).
42	    static let deloadFactor = 0.9
43	    /// Consecutive e1RM *drops* that count as regressing (needs N+1 sessions).
44	    static let regressionDeltas = 2
45	    /// Consecutive sessions without an e1RM *improvement* that count as a plateau.
46	    static let plateauDeltas = 3
47	
48	    /// The working rep range for double progression, per goal. Brackets the fixed
49	    /// prescription `PlanGenerator` writes (10 / 13 / 8 reps respectively).
50	    static func repRange(for goal: Goal) -> ClosedRange<Int> {
51	        switch goal {
52	        case .buildMuscle, .recomp: return 8...12
53	        case .loseWeight:           return 12...15
54	        case .sport:                return 6...10
55	        }
56	    }
57	
58	    /// Convenience over the primary rule table: rep range from the goal, weight step
59	    /// and reason formatting from the user's display units.
60	    static func recommend(exId: String,
61	                          history: [HistoryEntry],
62	                          goal: Goal,
63	                          units: Units = .kg) -> ProgressionRecommendation? {
64	        recommend(exId: exId,
65	                  history: history,
66	                  repRange: repRange(for: goal),
67	                  weightStepKg: Formulas.weightStepKg(units: units),
68	                  units: units)
69	    }
70	
71	    /// The rule table. History may arrive in any order (sorted by date internally);
72	    /// pass only entries for `exId`. Returns nil when there is nothing to base a
73	    /// recommendation on. Rules, first match wins:
74	    /// 1. Bodyweight lift (top weight 0) → progress by reps only (hold when stalling).
75	    /// 2. Top of the rep range reached → increase load, rebuild from the bottom.
76	    /// 3. e1RM dropped `regressionDeltas` sessions in a row → deload ~10%.
77	    /// 4. No e1RM improvement across `plateauDeltas` sessions → deload ~10%.
78	    /// 5. Latest session dipped (single off day, not yet a trend) → hold.
79	    /// 6. Otherwise → add a rep (double progression).
80	    static func recommend(exId: String,
81	                          history: [HistoryEntry],
82	                          repRange: ClosedRange<Int>,
83	                          weightStepKg: Double = 2.5,
84	                          units: Units = .kg) -> ProgressionRecommendation? {
85	        let sorted = history.sorted { $0.date < $1.date }
86	        guard let last = sorted.last else { return nil }
87	
88	        // Session-over-session e1RM deltas, oldest → newest.
89	        let series = sorted.map(\.e1rm)
90	        let deltas = zip(series.dropFirst(), series).map { $0 - $1 }
91	        let regressing = deltas.count >= regressionDeltas
92	            && deltas.suffix(regressionDeltas).allSatisfy { $0 < 0 }
93	        let plateaued = deltas.count >= plateauDeltas
94	            && deltas.suffix(plateauDeltas).allSatisfy { $0 <= 0 }
95	
96	        let weight = { (kg: Double) in Formulas.formatWeight(kg: kg, units: units) }
97	
98	        // Rule 1 — bodyweight: reps are the only lever, so the range top doesn't cap them.
99	        // e1RM is weight-based (always 0 here), so the stall signal comes from top reps.
100	        if last.topW == 0 {
101	            let repSeries = sorted.map(\.topR)
102	            let repDeltas = zip(repSeries.dropFirst(), repSeries).map { $0 - $1 }
103	            let repsRegressing = repDeltas.count >= regressionDeltas
104	                && repDeltas.suffix(regressionDeltas).allSatisfy { $0 < 0 }
105	            let repsPlateaued = repDeltas.count >= plateauDeltas
106	                && repDeltas.suffix(plateauDeltas).allSatisfy { $0 <= 0 }
107	            if repsRegressing || repsPlateaued {
108	                return ProgressionRecommendation(
109	                    exId: exId, action: .hold,
110	                    suggestedWeightKg: 0, suggestedReps: last.topR,
111	                    reason: "Progress has stalled — repeat \(last.topR) reps and focus on quality.")
112	            }
113	            return ProgressionRecommendation(
114	                exId: exId, action: .increaseReps,
115	                suggestedWeightKg: 0, suggestedReps: last.topR + 1,
116	                reason: "Add a rep — aim for \(last.topR + 1) next time.")
117	        }
118	
119	        // Rule 2 — range top reached: add load, rebuild reps from the bottom.
120	        if last.topR >= repRange.upperBound {
121	            let next = last.topW + weightStepKg
122	            return ProgressionRecommendation(
123	                exId: exId, action: .increaseLoad,
124	                suggestedWeightKg: next, suggestedReps: repRange.lowerBound,
125	                reason: "You hit \(last.topR) reps at \(weight(last.topW)) — " +
126	                        "move up to \(weight(next)) and rebuild from \(repRange.lowerBound) reps.")
127	        }
128	
129	        // Rules 3 & 4 — regression / plateau: take ~10% off and rebuild.
130	        if regressing || plateaued {
131	            let next = deloadWeight(fromKg: last.topW, stepKg: weightStepKg)
132	            let why = regressing
133	                ? "Est. 1RM has dropped \(regressionDeltas + 1) sessions in a row"
134	                : "No progress across your last \(plateauDeltas + 1) sessions"
135	            return ProgressionRecommendation(
136	                exId: exId, action: .deload,
137	                suggestedWeightKg: next, suggestedReps: repRange.lowerBound,
138	                reason: "\(why) — deload to \(weight(next)) and rebuild.")
139	        }
140	
141	        // Rule 5 — a single down session is noise, not a trend: repeat and consolidate.
142	        if let lastDelta = deltas.last, lastDelta < 0 {
143	            let reps = min(max(last.topR, repRange.lowerBound), repRange.upperBound)
144	            return ProgressionRecommendation(
145	                exId: exId, action: .hold,
146	                suggestedWeightKg: last.topW, suggestedReps: reps,
147	                reason: "Last session dipped — repeat \(weight(last.topW)) × \(reps) and consolidate.")
148	        }
149	
150	        // Rule 6 — double progression: same weight, one more rep (never below the range floor).
151	        let reps = max(min(last.topR + 1, repRange.upperBound), repRange.lowerBound)
152	        return ProgressionRecommendation(
153	            exId: exId, action: .increaseReps,
154	            suggestedWeightKg: last.topW, suggestedReps: reps,
155	            reason: "Progressing well — aim for \(weight(last.topW)) × \(reps).")
156	    }
157	
158	    /// ~10% off the working weight, snapped to the stepper increment, always strictly
159	    /// below the current weight (floored at 0).
160	    static func deloadWeight(fromKg kg: Double, stepKg: Double) -> Double {
161	        guard kg > 0 else { return 0 }
162	        let target = kg * deloadFactor
163	        guard stepKg > 0 else { return target }
164	        var snapped = (target / stepKg).rounded() * stepKg
165	        if snapped >= kg { snapped -= stepKg }
166	        return max(0, snapped)
167	    }
168	}

2	//  Coaching.swift
3	//  Replog
4	//
5	//  The trainer's durable memory. A `CoachingLog` is a dated, typed note the on-device
6	//  coach writes to itself — a progression recommendation, a detected plateau, a
7	//  bodyweight check-in, a published report — so it can "remember" context across weeks
8	//  and feed later reasoning (progression engine, weekly/monthly reports).
9	//
10	//  Like `HistoryEntry`, a log is a flat, queryable record: it references the catalog by
11	//  `exId` and a plan by `planId` (UUIDs, not relationships — matching `ActiveSession.workoutId`),
12	//  so the memory OUTLIVES the plan or exercise it once concerned. Structured detail rides
13	//  in a JSON payload, decoded on demand (the `HistoryEntry.sets` pattern).
14	//
15	
16	import Foundation
17	import SwiftData
18	
19	/// What a `CoachingLog` records. Drives filtering, iconography, and report grouping.
20	enum CoachingKind: String, Codable, CaseIterable, Identifiable, Sendable {
21	    /// A free-form coaching note.
22	    case note
23	    /// A load/rep recommendation for a specific lift (from the progression engine).
24	    case progression
25	    /// A detected stall across sessions.
26	    case plateau
27	    /// A recommended deload / back-off week.
28	    case deload
29	    /// A bodyweight check-in observation.
30	    case bodyweight
31	    /// A published weekly summary.
32	    case weeklyReport
33	    /// A published monthly rollup.
34	    case monthlyReport
35	    /// The coach adjusted the plan (split/volume/exercise choice).
36	    case planAdjustment
37	
38	    var id: String { rawValue }
39	
40	    var displayName: String {
41	        switch self {
42	        case .note:          return "Note"
43	        case .progression:   return "Progression"
44	        case .plateau:       return "Plateau"
45	        case .deload:        return "Deload"
46	        case .bodyweight:    return "Bodyweight"
47	        case .weeklyReport:  return "Weekly report"
48	        case .monthlyReport: return "Monthly report"
49	        case .planAdjustment: return "Plan adjustment"
50	        }
51	    }
52	}
53	
54	/// Structured detail for a `CoachingLog`, kept flexible so each `CoachingKind` can carry
55	/// only what it needs. Numeric facts (weights, e1RM, trend %, bodyweight) go in `metrics`;
56	/// short labels (recommended action verbs, muscle names) go in `tags`.
57	// Nonisolated: a pure value type whose Codable conformance must be usable inside the
58	// nonisolated JSONDecoder/JSONEncoder generics (the custom `init(from:)` would otherwise
59	// inherit the module's default MainActor isolation).
60	nonisolated struct CoachingPayload: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
61	    /// Named numeric facts, e.g. `["fromWeightKg": 60, "toWeightKg": 62.5, "trendPct": 4.1]`.
62	    var metrics: [String: Double]
63	    /// Short labels, e.g. `["increaseLoad"]` or `["chest", "triceps"]`.
64	    var tags: [String]
65	
66	    init(metrics: [String: Double] = [:], tags: [String] = []) {
67	        self.metrics = metrics
68	        self.tags = tags
69	    }
70	
71	    /// Lenient decoding so a bare `{}` (the model's default `payloadJSON`) and forward-compatible
72	    /// payloads that omit a field decode to sensible empties instead of throwing.
73	    init(from decoder: any Decoder) throws {
74	        let c = try decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
75	        self.metrics = try c.decodeIfPresent([String: Double].self, forKey: .metrics) ?? [:]
76	        self.tags = try c.decodeIfPresent([String].self, forKey: .tags) ?? []
77	    }
78	
79	    /// Convenience metric accessor (nil when absent).
80	    subscript(metric key: String) -> Double? { metrics[key] }
81	}
82	
83	@Model
84	final class CoachingLog {
85	    var id: UUID = UUID()
86	    var date: Date = Date()
87	    /// Stored as `CoachingKind.rawValue`; use `kind` for typed access.
88	    var kindRaw: String = CoachingKind.note.rawValue
89	    /// Human-readable one-liner (rendered in reports / a future coaching feed).
90	    var summary: String = ""
91	    /// The exercise this log concerns (`Exercise.id` in the static catalog), if any.
92	    var exId: String?
93	    /// The plan this log concerns, if any. A plain id reference (not a relationship) so the
94	    /// memory survives the plan's deletion.
95	    var planId: UUID?
96	    /// JSON-encoded `CoachingPayload` of structured detail.
97	    var payloadJSON: String = "{}"
98	
99	    init(
100	        kind: CoachingKind,
101	        summary: String,
102	        date: Date = Date(),
103	        exId: String? = nil,
104	        planId: UUID? = nil,
105	        payload: CoachingPayload = CoachingPayload()
106	    ) {
107	        self.kindRaw = kind.rawValue
108	        self.summary = summary
109	        self.date = date
110	        self.exId = exId
111	        self.planId = planId
112	        self.payload = payload
113	    }
114	
115	    var kind: CoachingKind {
116	        get { CoachingKind(rawValue: kindRaw) ?? .note }
117	        set { kindRaw = newValue.rawValue }
118	    }
119	
120	    /// Decoded structured payload.
121	    var payload: CoachingPayload {
122	        get { (try? JSONDecoder().decode(CoachingPayload.self, from: Data(payloadJSON.utf8))) ?? CoachingPayload() }
123	        set { payloadJSON = String(data: (try? JSONEncoder().encode(newValue)) ?? Data("{}".utf8), encoding: .utf8) ?? "{}" }
124	    }
125	}

16	    /// Builds and inserts an ActiveSession for `workout`. The caller saves the context.

18	    static func start(workout: Workout, into context: ModelContext) -> ActiveSession {

4	//
5	//  Finishing a workout: write each exercise's top set to History, bump the streak,
6	//  mark today complete on the calendar, then remove the live session.
7	//
8	
9	import Foundation
10	import SwiftData
11	
12	@MainActor
13	enum SessionFinisher {
14	
15	    /// Result of finishing, useful for tests/UI feedback.
16	    struct Summary: Equatable {
17	        var exercisesLogged: Int
18	        var newStreak: Int
19	        var weekStreak: Int
20	        /// Whether the workout was fully completed (and therefore counted toward streaks).
21	        var countedAsComplete: Bool
22	    }
23	
24	    /// Persists history for every exercise with at least one completed set. Only a *fully
25	    /// completed* workout counts toward the streaks and the lifetime total: a partial finish
26	    /// still saves progress (history) but does not mark the scheduled day done, so the
27	    /// schedule-aware streak can break. Always recomputes both streaks, then deletes the session.
28	    @discardableResult
29	    static func finish(_ session: ActiveSession, profile: UserProfile,
30	                       context: ModelContext, date: Date = Date()) -> Summary {
31	        let isComplete = session.isComplete
32	
33	        var logged = 0
34	        for exercise in session.exercises {
35	            let doneSets = exercise.sets.filter(\.done)
36	            guard !doneSets.isEmpty else { continue }
37	            let top = doneSets.max {
38	                Formulas.e1rm(kg: $0.weightKg, reps: $0.reps) < Formulas.e1rm(kg: $1.weightKg, reps: $1.reps)
39	            }!
40	            let entry = HistoryEntry(
41	                exId: exercise.exId,
42	                date: date,
43	                topW: top.weightKg,
44	                topR: top.reps,
45	                e1rm: Formulas.e1rmRounded(kg: top.weightKg, reps: top.reps),
46	                sets: doneSets.sorted { $0.order < $1.order }.map { RecordedSet(w: $0.weightKg, r: $0.reps) }
47	            )
48	            context.insert(entry)
49	            logged += 1
50	        }
51	
52	        if isComplete {
53	            profile.totalWorkouts += 1
54	            profile.doneDates = StreakCalendar.recordingCompletion(date, into: profile.doneDates)
55	        }
56	        context.recomputeStreaks(profile: profile, today: date)
57	
58	        let summary = Summary(
59	            exercisesLogged: logged,
60	            newStreak: profile.streak,
61	            weekStreak: profile.weekStreak,
62	            countedAsComplete: isComplete
63	        )
64	        context.delete(session)
65	        try? context.save()
66	        return summary
67	    }
68	}

9	import Foundation
10	import SwiftData
11	
12	enum ReplogSchema {
13	    /// All persisted model types.
14	    static let models: [any PersistentModel.Type] = [
15	        Plan.self, Workout.self, PlanItem.self, SetTemplate.self,
16	        ActiveSession.self, SessionExercise.self, LoggedSet.self,
17	        HistoryEntry.self, UserProfile.self, AppSettings.self,

20	
21	    /// The app's on-disk container.
22	    /// On a fresh device install `Library/Application Support` may not exist yet, which
23	    /// makes SwiftData fail to create its store ("Failed to create file; code = 2"). We
24	    /// create that directory first, then open the store; if the store itself is corrupt
25	    /// or schema-incompatible (e.g. left over from an older build), we wipe it once and
26	    /// retry, falling back to in-memory as a last resort so the app always launches.
27	    @MainActor
28	    static func container() -> ModelContainer {
29	        let schema = Schema(models)
30	        let config = ModelConfiguration(isStoredInMemoryOnly: false)
31	        let storeURL = config.url
32	
33	        // Ensure the store's parent directory exists.
34	        try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(
35	            at: storeURL.deletingLastPathComponent(),
36	            withIntermediateDirectories: true
37	        )
38	
39	        if let c = try? ModelContainer(for: schema, configurations: config) { return c }
40	
41	        // Genuine corruption / incompatible schema: remove the store files and retry once.
42	        for suffix in ["", "-shm", "-wal"] {
43	            try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: URL(fileURLWithPath: storeURL.path + suffix))
44	        }
